crop.notes: Whole article from headline decks to 'The Close' (spans 13 pieces). The bottom also carries two unrelated short items, 'Meat-Shop Cases in Police Court' and 'Application for Pardon', plus an ad.

ocr.notes: Transcript stops at 'The Ground for the Ring' (about a third of the article); the ring-making, both fights and the close are missing. Errors in the part present: 'Charley Satine' for Charley Gallagher, 'Cy Sayers ... Henry Sayers' for George Seddons ... Henry Reinsaeder, 'Carey' for Carty, 'Pat. Malloy' for Pat. Hafford, 'faro bank' for 'bank of chuck-a-luck', boat hirers given wrongly (image: Dick Roche, Mike McCoole and Jack Looney).

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported two prize fights on Carroll Island below St. Louis: Tom Allen seconded George Seddons to victory over John Lafferty in 19 rounds, then seconded George Carey and threw up the sponge after 14 rounds against James C. Gallagher.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, January 26, 1870. The fights were 'yesterday', January 25, 1870. Article runs pg 3, cols 5-6.

facts.fact: Allen seconded George Seddons (with Patsey Curtin) in his fight with John Lafferty for $500 a side on Carroll Island, Illinois, about twelve miles below St. Louis; Seddons won in 19 rounds, 43 minutes
places: Carroll Island, Illinois (Mississippi River below St. Louis)

facts.fact: Allen seconded George Carey (with Patsey Curtin) against James C. Gallagher of Albany, N.Y., for a $50 purse on Carroll Island; Allen threw up the sponge for Carey after 14 rounds, 18 minutes
The paper recalled that Allen had been 'knocked out of time' by Charley Gallagher on the same spot, by the old distillery on Carroll Island, 'last summer'

notes: Passengers discussed the coming Mace-Allen fight. The paper's 'last summer' for the Allen-Gallagher loss may be wrong; check against the fight record. Allen is a second, not a principal, so focus is secondary.
